language.conditions: Ordinary persistent InnoDB with stock foreign_key_checks=1, utf8mb4 and empty sql_mode.

rules.owner: The ALTER target uses the session-visible table identity. Only a persistent InnoDB table with a settled field and physical index inventory admits these table-level additions.
rules.parent: An unqualified parent belongs to the child database. A qualified parent has its stated database. Both bind in the persistent dictionary, including when a like-named temporary relation exists or the default database differs. All labels retain canonical spelling.
rules.pairs: Check one through sixteen full fields ordered and paired by position, each side distinct under native identifier case. Require the same native integer width and signedness for the bounded integer domain. BOOL aliases signed TINYINT; SERIAL is unsigned BIGINT. Prefix fields and legacy explicit sort directions refuse. Modern DESC contributes to the physical ordering of a generated child index.
rules.parentIndex: Use the original physical reference coordinates. MySQL 5.6 through 8.3 admit eligible full leading prefixes including applicable hidden clustered fields. MySQL 8.4 and later require an exact unique or primary key under the stock restriction. A new generated index does not satisfy a missing original parent key in a self-reference.
rules.childIndex: Require the exact ordered full original prefix and native child direction for reuse. Hidden clustered suffix fields do not suppress an explicit generated creation. Prune generated proposals covered by original keys or by a retained longer compatible proposal. Retain the later of equal uncovered proposals. A retained proposal takes the explicit constraint symbol, then the index label, then a name from the first canonical child field and checked fallback suffix.
rules.constraints: An explicit symbol and a generated name identify the added edge in the persistent child database. Constraint and index names are separate namespaces with different checks. Resolve collisions belonging to any persistent table in the child database.
rules.generatedNames: The ordinary generated symbol uses the original child spelling, _ibfk_, and the next ordinal after the highest eligible preexisting marker on that table. Matching the generated prefix is case-sensitive. A leading-zero or nonnumeric suffix is not an ordinal. Explicit selected symbols in the same group do not increase the starting ordinal. Keep the native written group order for autogenerated names.
rules.effects: Validate the mode and closed effect roles before publication. Actual child rows can cause a defined execution-time integrity refusal. On MySQL 5.6 ALTER IGNORE remains a separate checked option and preserves enforcement.

observations: Exact persistent owners and parent column coordinates, order, and NULL effects
Native constraint names, metadata and matching logical rules
Original and resulting qualified physical keys with more than one pair, direction, and reuse versus allocation
Actual parent writes and child rows, including unresolved catalog refusal and data-dependent native rejection
Effective DDL transaction behavior and exact diagnostic categories

finite.requirement: Separate finite domains with expected coordinates and semantic coverage reconciled outside the producer.

faults: Use the default schema as the parent of an unqualified reference
Bind a parent to a temporary shadow
Reuse a constraint from an unrelated earlier prefix
Omit an earlier or later pair in the emitted statement
Replace effective parent actions or omit a lexical role under the corresponding release
trackedBeyondInitialIntegerGroup: Generated and non-integer key field profiles, including observed decimal encodings and collation families
ALTER forms mixing addition with dropping or renaming native keys or constraints
Legacy length corner cases containing truncated protocol names and database-encoded identities
Outlier automatic ordinal wraparound and affected legacy temporary dictionary artifacts
Mode changes that allow InnoDB online addition under disabled referential checks
trust: Complete accurately interpreted native schema facts and the specified stock language profile
The future independent executable verifier, its native fixture environment and the human-reviewed protected reference
